meta.claims_class: MODELED COST input quality; NO fill/queue/execution-realism claims

schema.publication_fields_note: no publisher_id/sequence/ts_init in these trimmed parquet exports (absent, not null)

boundary.note: file ranges touch at 2023-10-01; not re-verified row-level for duplicates here (bulk coverage out of D5 scope)

stamp_convention.conclusion: ts_event = bar interval START: no bar stamped 16:00-16:59 (maintenance halt); reopen trades at 17:00:00 CT appear in the 17:00-stamped bar; last session bar stamped 15:59

front_selection.rule: front = highest 1m-volume outright instrument per session (schema-lane approximation; T-5 roll not needed for schema work)

settlement.source: AV1T-statistics-ALL10 (statistics schema), stat_type=3 SETTLEMENT_PRICE per databento_dbn StatType enum
settlement.note_close_price_stat: stat_type 11 CLOSE_PRICE: zero ES rows in sampled chunks (absent for ES; SETTLEMENT_PRICE is the mark CME publishes for ES)

ibkr_volume_ratio.note: vendor sum(1m trade volume)/IBKR daily volume; 1m volume semantics = traded contracts per minute

ibkr_reproduction.definition: IBKR daily ASK-close minus BID-close, same session, front ESZ6, last 20 mutual sessions (mirrors fut10 spread_stats close-to-close BID/ASK proxy)

vendor_1m_analogue.note: vendor has TRADE ohlcv only (no BBO owned): a BID/ASK-close proxy CANNOT be mirrored. Reported instead: consecutive-1m |dclose| in ticks (effective-cost flavored, floor-ish) and 1m high-low range (volatility flavored, upper bound flavor) on the same sessions.

spread_proxy.honest_statement: A close-proxy spread supports ONLY tiering inputs for modeled cost with an overstatement caveat (IBKR daily BID/ASK closes are two non-synchronous marks; the 15:00/16:00 convention gap above shows single-time marks can sit ~ticks away from each other). It does NOT support execution realism claims, fill probability, queue position, or capacity: bbo-1m is NOT owned and, per Co-Owner, insufficient anyway. Vendor 1m |dclose| likewise bounds nothing executable — it only shows the ES front trades on a 1-tick grid with ~half of minute transitions flat, consistent with a ~1-tick effective-spread regime.
